newsitem.title: UK: LME options spotlight on copper, others neglected.
newsitem.headline: LME options spotlight on copper, others neglected.

text.p: Volatility in LME copper options ticked higher this week on the back of a futures rally to 13-month highs.
Another big lump of options turnover on Thursday, however, was probably another give-up among brokers since open interest failed to rise in tandem, traders said.
The futures rally was fuelled by covering of exposed options positions and some traders said the main player was Korea's LG Metals.
The firm on Friday said it had been conducting futures and options operations to hedge risks from its physical metal trades, but declined to give details.
On the LME on Thursday, nearby copper options traded up to 23.5 percent implied volatility, traders said.

At-the-money (ATM) volatility was quoted on Friday morning for July at around 21.0/23.0 percent, up about two points from Monday, when three month futures prices were moribund under $2,500. August was around 20.0/22.0 percent.
Much of the activity was in nearby upside calls, but there was also interest in puts, traders said.
"It seems $2,600, $2,650 and $2,700 nearbys were the flavour of the month this week," one trader said.
"But downside puts were in demand for first and second quarter 1998 and were demanding a premium of one-half vol for each $100 premium," he added. Most popular strikes were $2,000 and $2,100.
Another trader said $2,200s were sought for 4th quarter 1998.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, LME data showed large turnover in $2,450 and $2,550 puts for September 1997. During the two days, open interest rose by 800 lots (equivalent to 20,000 tonnes) on each of the two strikes.
Another trader said there had been a lot of enquiry for cheap downside puts as futures prices steamed higher, but players were wary of granting them.
"I think a lot of people have learned their lesson," he said.
He was referring to big option losses some firms incurred when the bottom fell out of the market a year ago when the Sumitomo crisis erupted and exposed put positions suddenly came into the money.
Overall activity was heavy on Thursday, when three month prices shot up to a 13-month peak of $2,609, but not as big as official turnover figures indicated, traders said.

LME data showed total volume of 20,919 lots but open interest rose by only 4,305 lots. "It's got to be another give-up among brokers...It's now become de-rigeur to have these huge volumes every so often," one trader said.
Most of the other metals took a backseat to copper, but one trader said some buying was seen in aluminium and the vols should be bottoming out.
The buying was for next year ATM options, he added.
Vols were little changed, with July and August quoted around 15.5/17.5 percent and the average of 1998 at 14.75/15.25 percent.
Another trader said some interest had been shown in zinc for put buying on the bet that the futures are due for a correction.
The enquiries were for $1,300 and $1,325 puts for August, he added.
